title: onprem/airgap: add rke2 ubuntu-22.04 arm64 offline bundle + apt-mirror & rollback tooling
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: Add first-class support for building an on-prem/offline bundle targeting RKE2 clusters on Ubuntu 22.04 (arm64) and include an opinionated apt-mirror and rollback helper so customers can reliably install and roll back the private installer in air-gapped environments. This change is driven by customer requests (SUP-8876) and internal partner testing on arm64 nodes.

What this PR does: builds on existing vendoring infra to produce a minimal offline bundle for rke2+ubuntu-22.04-arm64 with: apt repository snapshots, kernel module packages pinned to supported kernel-sets, containerd and rke2 binaries vendored, helm charts pre-packaged, and a small apt-mirror service with config snippets that can be bootstrapped from the airgap bundle. Adds a rollback/restore helper script and an upgrade plan template for cluster operators.

Key changes (high level):
- packaging: offline-bundles/rke2/ubuntu-22.04/arm64/ added (tar layout, checksums, manifest.json pointer)
- vendoring: scripts/vendor/apt-mirror-builder.sh extended to support arm64 package fetch and tarring
- installer: installer/airgap/apt-mirror-configs/ubuntu-22.04/ templates and systemd unit for local mirror service
- helm: charts/redwood-private-installer/values-airgap-ubuntu-22.04.yaml updated to include apt-mirror bootstrap bits
- terraform: modules/airgap-setup/apt-mirror module updated to allow arm64 AMI selection and local mirror lifecycler resources
- tooling: tools/rollback/rollback-helper.sh added, with documented safe-rollback steps and dry-run mode
- docs: docs/onprem/airgap/ubuntu-22.04-arm64.md added with upgrade/rollback guidance and validation checklist

Testing performed:
- Local CI: unit tests for vendor scripts and linter pass.
- Integration: built offline bundle in CI runner (arm64 runner), deployed to a k3s->rke2 test cluster in our private lab (arm64 nodes) using the installer in airgap mode; verified installer completes, apt-mirror serves packages, services start, and application image pull flows succeed via local mirror.
- Rollback smoke test: applied upgrade then used rollback-helper.sh in dry-run and execute modes; validated state restored and no orphaned resources remain.

Backward compatibility: This is additive; existing installer flows for amd64/other distros are unchanged. The apt-mirror module exposes the same variables and retains default values.

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- Add CI job that periodically re-builds arm64 offline bundles and uploads to staging bundles bucket. (ENG-4199)
- Add automated tests to validate package checksums against distro mirrors on new kernel releases.

Notes on security and SBOM: All vendored packages include a generated SBOM and sha256 checksums in the bundle manifest. The apt-mirror-builder includes an optional verify mode to cross-check upstream signatures before bundling.

release_notes: Add RKE2 Ubuntu 22.04 (arm64) offline bundle and apt-mirror + rollback tooling for on-prem air-gapped installer. Includes SBOMs and manifest checksums. Opt-in terraform ami_arm64_enabled variable added.
notes: This PR targets private installer customers who need arm64 air-gap support. The bundle size is ~1.2GB compressed; users should plan mirror disk accordingly. The terraform change is opt-in by default to avoid breaking existing infra.
